title: Stage 2 ION business case and speed cameras
subtitle: Airport growth plan, RetrofitWR funding, Lancaster Street expropriation, water financial plans and Homer Watson road designation.
overview: The committee heard preliminary results of the Stage 2 ION initial business case, which compares full light rail, partial light rail and bus rapid transit options for reaching Cambridge. Staff said full light rail and full bus rapid transit are the two strongest options, and that a recommendation will come to Council in November. The committee also received updates on the airport growth plan, which is going to public consultation, and on the municipal speed camera program's first six months. All three were received for information.

Through the consent agenda, the committee recommended that Council approve the Water Financial Plans, the assumption of Oxford Road 5 in Wilmot, and delegated authority to sign agreements for the RetrofitWR home-energy loan pilot {{vote:m2}}. It also recommended expropriating land for Phase 1 of the Lancaster Street West improvements in Kitchener {{vote:m6}}, and adding frontage at 2400 Homer Watson Boulevard to the Regional road system {{vote:m7}}.
These items affect future transit options and costs, road safety enforcement, home retrofit financing and road projects. Council makes the final decisions on all recommendations.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the Water Financial Plans set out in report EES-WWO-25-003 under Ontario Regulation 453-07.

The committee recommended that Council delegate authority to staff to sign the Federation of Canadian Municipalities financing agreement, an administration agreement with GrandBridge Energy, and loan agreements with participating homeowners.

The committee recommended that Council approve expropriating partial takings and temporary grading easements at three Kitchener properties for Phase 1 of the Lancaster Street West (Regional Road 29) improvements.
The committee recommended a by-law adding lands at the frontage of 2400 Homer Watson Boulevard to Regional Road 28, with notice registered on title.
The committee recommended that Council approve the actions in Appendix A to assume Oxford Road 5 in Wilmot.

debate: A delegate from a transit advocacy group urged light rail all the way to downtown Cambridge. The delegate also urged building it in smaller pieces with in-house project management to hold down costs, and asking senior governments for program-level funding.

Township councillors asked whether township taxpayers will help pay for Stage 2. Staff said operating costs are area-rated but that capital area-rating needs further review. One councillor said the cities gain tax benefits the townships do not, while staff said roads have not been area-rated either, so the full mobility picture matters.

On Stage 2, councillors asked about funding, express service and township bus links. Staff said they will seek full senior-government funding but could build in phases, and that the Delta station option has limited development potential and terminal space.

On speed cameras, some councillors said the 24-hour operation, ticket affordability and the largely online appeal process were unfair. Others called the stunt-driving numbers alarming, and some questioned whether a monetary penalty is enough and asked for more transparency on ticket thresholds. Staff said they would look at appeals, school-zone timing and affordability if directed.

Supporters said the program slows drivers and that money above operating costs goes into a road safety reserve, which is not funded from the tax levy. Staff said cancelling the program would bring contract costs and staff reallocation.
